### Biography of Billy Halligan

William "Billy" Halligan (18 February 1886 – 1950) was an Irish professional footballer who played as a centre forward. Born in Athlone, Ireland, Halligan began his career in his homeland before moving to England, where he played for several Football League clubs. He also had a brief stint with non-league teams towards the end of his career. Notably, while playing for Nelson, he scored the club's first-ever goal in the Football League, in a 1–2 loss to Wigan Borough on 27 August 1921 [Data: Infobox football biography 2].

### Club Career

Halligan's senior career started in Ireland with Cliftonville and Belfast Celtic. In 1908, he joined Distillery, where he played for one season. During this time, he was noticed by Leeds City, who signed him at the beginning of the 1909–10 season. Halligan quickly made an impact, scoring two goals on his debut in a 5–0 victory against Lincoln City on 1 September 1909. Over the course of the season, he scored 12 goals, helping Leeds City avoid relegation from the Football League Second Division [Data: Infobox football biography 2].

His performances caught the attention of Derby County, who signed him for a fee of £400 in February 1910. Halligan played 22 games for Derby County, scoring eight goals before moving to Wolverhampton Wanderers in June 1911 for £450. At Wolverhampton, he continued to impress, scoring 19 goals in his first season and 15 goals in his second season. In May 1913, he transferred to Hull City for £600, where he scored 28 goals in 65 games over two seasons [Data: Infobox football biography 2].

During World War I, Halligan played for various teams as a guest, including Manchester United, Chesterfield, and Stockport County. After the war, he joined Preston North End in 1919, scoring two goals in 16 matches. He then moved to Oldham Athletic on a free transfer in January 1920, scoring six goals in 18 league games. The following season, he made only ten league appearances, scoring three goals as Oldham finished 19th in the Football League First Division [Data: Infobox football biography 2].

In August 1922, Halligan joined Nelson for the club's first season in the Football League Third Division North. He scored Nelson's first-ever Football League goal on his debut, in a 1–2 loss to Wigan Borough on 27 August 1921. He left Nelson in June 1922 and joined Boston Town, before moving to Wisbech Town in 1924. Halligan retired at the end of the 1924–25 season, aged 39 [Data: Infobox football biography 2].

### International Career

Halligan represented the Ireland national football team, earning two caps and scoring one goal. His first cap and goal came on 28 January 1911, in a 1–2 loss to Wales. His second appearance for Ireland was on 10 February 1912, in a 1–6 loss to England. Post-World War I, he played in two unofficial Victory international matches for Ireland, including a 1–2 defeat to Scotland on 22 March 1919 and a 0–0 draw in the return match on 19 April 1919 [Data: Infobox football biography 2].

Billy Halligan's career spanned over two decades, showcasing his talent and adaptability across various levels of English and Irish football. His contributions to the clubs he played for and his international appearances highlight his significant role in early 20th-century football history.

'''Jan Vertonghen''' (born 24 April 1987 in [[Sint-Niklaas]], [[Belgium]]) is a [[Belgium|Belgian]] [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre back|centre back]] for [[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[Eredivisie]] club, [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]]. A left-footed player, he equally adept at playing at left-back and left midfield and frequently joins in the attack from his centre back position.

== Club career ==
=== Ajax ===
After spending time at VK Tielrode and [[Germinal Beerschot]], Vertonghen moved to the [[Netherlands]] and signed a contract with the youth academy of [[Eredivisie]] side [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]]. He began as a midfielder but now he mostly plays at centre back for Ajax.<ref>{{citenews|title=Jan Vertonghen tevreden met positie bij Ajax|url=http://www.voetbalcentraal.nl/nieuws/39673/jan-vertonghen-tevreden-met-positie-bij-ajax-list|publisher=voetcalcentraal.nl|date=12 November 2009|language=Dutch}}</ref> During his time in the [[Jong Ajax|reserves]], he became known for an incident in the [[KNVB Cup 2005-06|2006 KNVB Cup]] game against [[Cambuur Leeuwarden]], his first ever home game at the [[Amsterdam ArenA]], where he "scored" a bizarre goal to put Ajax 3-0 up. He had attempted a back pass to the Cambuur goalkeeper while a teammate was receiving treatment but instead the ball sailed past the shocked goalkeeper, much to the amusement of the spectators and the bewilderment of the players.<ref>{{citenews|title=Gatorade Cup: Young Ajax beat Cambuur in memorable game|url=http://www.ajaxusa.com/news/2005-2006/gatorade-cup-young-ajax-beat-cambuur-in-memorable-game.html|publisher=Ajax USA|date=20 September 2005}}</ref>

In a 6-0 win over [[Willem II Tilburg|Willem II]] in the [[Amsterdam ArenA]], Vertonghen made his professional debut on [[December 3]], [[2006]]. He would play another two matches for the first half of the season. After the winter break, he was sent on loan to struggling [[RKC Waalwijk]] for the remainder of the season. At RKC Waalwijk he would play 12 matches in which he scored three times, but he was unable to help them avoid relegation to the [[Eerste Divisie]].

Vertonghen returned to Ajax for the 2007-08 season, where he was tipped for stardom, but was unable to break through, due to a bad injury as well as the presence of [[John Heitinga]] and [[Thomas Vermaelen]]. [[Johan Cruyff]] has made no secret of his admiration for the left-footed youngster who can handle any left-sided position in defence and midfield. On 26 September 2008 he extended his contract to [[30 June]] [[2013]]. 

The 2008-09 season was a breakthrough season for the young defender. After Heitinga left for [[Atlético Madrid]], Vertonghen became Vermaelen's first choice partner in central defence. He started in 23 of the 26 games he played and scored 4 goals. On 28 September, he scored a rare double against [[Vitesse Arnhem|Vitesse]] in a 3-0 win. Although sustaining an injury from training during the week, he played in the 24 January match against [[FC Groningen]], billed as a "must-win" match by coach Marco van Basten<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/preview?id=249496&cc=3888&league=NED.1 Preview: FC Groningen vs Ajax Amsterdam]</ref>, and was unfortunate enough to be sent off for two yellow cards as Ajax lost 1-0. He was out for a month after sustaining a hamstring injury in the 1 March win away at [[FC Utrecht|Utrecht]] but his return lasted only several games as his season was prematurely ended after picking up another injury.

Under new coach [[Martin Jol]], Vertonghen retained his place in the starting line-up for the 2009-10 season. Despite injuring his toe while on international duty against Spain the previous week, he scored his first goal of the season, a penalty, in a 6-0 thrashing of [[NAC Breda]] on 13 September.<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=271828&cc=3888&league=NED.1 Report: Ajax Amsterdam vs NAC Breda]</ref> With the departure of Vermaelen to Arsenal, he now regularly partners fellow Belgian [[Toby Alderweireld]] in central defence.<ref>[http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind=1/newsid=893463.html Ajax set new goals in Europe]</ref><ref>{{citenews|title=Jol: 'Vertonghen is een echte Hollander'|url=http://www.gva.be/nieuws/sport/video/extern-jol-vertonghen-is-een-echte-hollander.aspx|publisher=Gazet van Antwerpen|date=26 September 2009|accessdate=27 October 2009|language=Dutch}}</ref>

== International career ==
Vertonghen was called up for the U21's and played in the [[2007 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship|2007 UEFA U21 Championships]]. On 21 June 2007 he made his debut in the senior debut for the [[Belgium national football team|national team]] in a 2-1 loss to [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]]. He was also selected for the 2008 Olympics and played in every match as the Belgians unexpectedly took fourth place. 

In the [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2010 World Cup qualifying]], he began to establish himself as a regular, initially at centre back as former Ajax teammate [[Thomas Vermaelen]]'s partner. # Jan Vertonghen: A Versatile Belgian Defender

## Biography

Jan Vertonghen, born on April 24, 1987, in Sint-Niklaas, Belgium, is a professional footballer who primarily plays as a centre back. Standing at 1.89 meters tall, Vertonghen is known for his versatility, capable of playing as a left-back or left midfielder as well. He currently plays for AFC Ajax in the Eredivisie, wearing the number 5 jersey. His career path began in the youth academies of VK Tielrode, Germinal Beerschot, and eventually Ajax, where he transitioned from a midfielder to a defender.

## Club Career

### Early Years at Ajax

Vertonghen joined Ajax's youth academy in 2003 and quickly made a name for himself. One notable incident occurred during his debut at the Amsterdam Arena in the 2006 KNVB Cup game against Cambuur Leeuwarden, where he inadvertently scored a bizarre goal by attempting a back pass to the goalkeeper. This amusing moment highlighted his potential and adaptability on the field.

### Professional Debut and Loan Spell

On December 3, 2006, Vertonghen made his professional debut for Ajax in a 6-0 victory over Willem II. However, his opportunities were limited in the first half of the season. In the second half, he was loaned to RKC Waalwijk, where he played 12 matches and scored three goals, though he couldn't prevent the team from being relegated to the Eerste Divisie.

### Breakthrough Season

Returning to Ajax for the 2007-08 season, Vertonghen faced competition from established defenders like John Heitinga and Thomas Vermaelen. Despite this, he managed to extend his contract until 2013. The 2008-09 season marked a significant breakthrough for him. After Heitinga's departure to Atlético Madrid, Vertonghen became Vermaelen's regular partner in central defense. He started in 23 of the 26 games he played and scored four goals, including a rare double against Vitesse.

### Recent Seasons

Under Martin Jol's coaching in the 2009-10 season, Vertonghen continued to be a key player despite injuries. He scored his first goal of the season in a 6-0 win over NAC Breda. With Vermaelen's departure to Arsenal, Vertonghen often partnered Toby Alderweireld in central defense.

## International Career

Vertonghen has represented Belgium at various levels, including the U21 team and the senior national team. He made his senior debut on June 21, 2007, in a 2-1 loss to Portugal. He also participated in the 2008 Olympics, helping Belgium achieve an unexpected fourth-place finish.

In the 2010 World Cup qualifiers, Vertonghen established himself as a regular player, initially partnering with Thomas Vermaelen. He scored his first international goal in a friendly against the Czech Republic in August 2009. However, he suffered an injury against Spain in September 2009, which sidelined him for two weeks. Currently, he often plays in midfield as Daniel Van Buyten and Vermaelen are the preferred central defenders.

'''Fabien Alain Barthez''' (born 28 June 1971 in [[Lavelanet]]) is a former French [[association football|football]] [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] who won honours with [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and the [[France national football team|French national team]], with whom he won the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] and [[2000 UEFA European Football Championship|Euro 2000]] and reached the final of the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]]. He shares the record for the most [[FIFA World Cup records#Goalkeeping|World Cup finals clean sheets]] with [[Peter Shilton]], with 10. Professionally, he has kept goal for his clubs to a [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] title and several [[Ligue 1]] and [[Premier League]] titles.

==Club career==
===Marseille===
Born in [[Lavelanet]], [[France]], Barthez made his first division debut for [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] on 21 September 1991, against [[AS Nancy|Nancy]]. He joined [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] in 1992, and won both the French championship and the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] at the end of his first season in Marseille. His performance in the final against [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] was one of the best ever seen for a goalkeeper,{{Fact|date=November 2008}} and the 1993 victory made him the youngest goalkeeper to win a Champions League title until [[Iker Casillas]] did so in 2000.

However, Marseille would be stripped of their domestic title, though not of the Champions League crown, due to their involvement in a domestic [[match fixing]] scandal, and a year later (1994) would suffer a forced relegation to the second division due to a related financial bankruptcy. Barthez's 1993-94 season is seen by many as his best in [[le Championnat]],{{Fact|date=November 2008}} his many saves and the goalscoring quality of [[Sonny Anderson]] allowed l'OM to finish second this year. He stayed with the club in Division 2 for the 1994-95 season despite many offers from elite French clubs.<ref>http://www.eurosport.fr/football/story_sto979355.shtml</ref>

===AS Monaco===
In 1995, Barthez joined [[AS Monaco FC|AS Monaco]] and won [[Ligue 1]] titles in 1997 and 2000.

===Manchester United===
As a result of Barthez's success in the World Cup and Euro, he caught the attention of [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] manager [[Alex Ferguson]], who was searching for a star goalkeeper to replace the recently-departed [[Peter Schmeichel]]. Barthez joined United for £7.8 million in 2000. He was later reunited with national team-mate [[Laurent Blanc]] who joined Manchester United in 2001. The Barthez-Blanc head-kissing ritual was performed at the start of Champions League matches.

Well-known for being eccentric<ref>http://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/fabien-barthez-the-goalkeepers-fear-of-losing-it-618203.html</ref>, Barthez started out well for Manchester United. His first season was a triumph as he answered all the questions about how he would handle rainy Manchester compared to sunny Monaco. Barthez performed brilliantly throughout the season and became a crowd favourite. The fans loved his eccentric behaviour, his taunting dribbles and step-overs past opposing strikers, and most importantly, his remarkable reaction saves.{{Fact|date=November 2008}} Very often it was critical saves that kept United from defeat or dropping valuable points, helping United to the 2000-01 Premier League title, their third in a row. The only blemish being his failed attempt at "psyching out" West Ham United's [[Paolo Di Canio]] in the FA Cup 4th Round. Di Canio beat the offside trap, while Barthez stood still with his hand up expecting the referee to blow his whistle, or Di Canio to stop. Di Canio continued and scored the only goal of the game.

The 2001-02 season was split into two parts for him.  The first half was a nightmare. The Frenchman seemed to be taking some unnecessary risks outside his penalty area, and his antics began to have consequences that allowed unneeded goals for opposing teams. He was at fault for two goals in a home defeat by [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] in October 2001, <ref>Anderson, D. (2001). [http://www.redcafe.net/archives/report.php?id=272 Manchester United 2:3 Deportivo La Coruna.] RedCafe.net - Unofficial Manchester United Website. Retrieved on July 6 2006.</ref> Another couple of errors against Arsenal the following month put much pressure on Barthez. There was much speculation as to what was the source of Barthez's decline, and critics urged him to be dropped. However, Sir Alex Ferguson had faith in his goalkeeper and stuck by him. Consequently in the second half of the season, Barthez repaired his reputation with consistent, solid performances and the spectacular saves that he was famous for.

In 2002-2003 led to another Premier League cromywn for United. The season was a mixed bag for Barthez. One highlight was a fabulous save to deny [[Dietmar Hamann]]'s 30 yard rocket at Anfield as United held on to win 2-1. In other games, he let goals go past him that shouldn't have done. Barthez was also widely criticised in United's exit to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] in the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], especially for [[Ronaldo]]'s opener which beat him at the near post.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/champions_league/2971519.stm]</ref> It would prove to be his last ever game with United as Sir Alex Ferguson's patience had finally run out. Barthez was dropped for the final 3 games of the season, with [[Roy Carroll]] taking his place.

However, [[FIFA]] blocked the loan deal on the grounds that it was not agreed upon within the international [[transfer window]]. The two clubs agreed on a loan deal after the transfer window reopened on 1 January 2004, and Barthez joined Marseille soon afterwards. '''Guillermo Luis Franco Farcuason''', commonly known as '''Guille Franco''' (born 3 November 1976) is a [[Argentina|Argentinian]]-born [[Mexico|Mexican]] [[Association football|football]] player who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]]. He is currently contracted to [[West Ham United|West Ham United]], and also plays for the [[Mexico national football team|Mexico national team]].

==Early Life==
Guille Franco was born in [[Corrientes]], the capital city of the [[Corrientes Province|homonymous province]] in [[Argentina]].
 
== Career ==
Franco began his career with [[Primera División Argentina|Argentine first division]] side [[Club Atlético San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]], playing with the team from 1996 to 2002. Franco then joined [[C.F. Monterrey|Monterrey]] in the middle of 2002, and made his debut during the 2002 [[Apertura]].  Franco was very successful with the ''Rayados'', and led the league in scoring during the 2004 Apertura with 15 goals in 16 games. He was in the team which won the [[Primera División de México|championship]] in 2003 and achieved runner-up position twice in 2004 and 2005.

Franco spent 3 years in Spain, playing for [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] but his spell was plagued with injury<ref>[http://www.transfermarkt.de/de/news/31412/g-franco-zu-west-ham.html G. Franco zu West Ham]</ref>. Franco was, however, the scorer of a goal by which Villarreal qualified for the [[UEFA Cup]] in a 1-0 victory against [[Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]].

In September 2009 Franco signed for [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] on a one year contract, becoming the first Mexican to sign for the Hammers.<ref>[http://www.whufc.com/page/News/0,,12562~1794381,00.html Franco signs] www.whufc.com</ref>On 25 September it was disclosed that due to West Ham's perilous financial situation following former chairman [[Björgólfur Guðmundsson]]'s financial collapse, West Ham's [[CEO]] Scott Duxbury, and their Sporting and Football Technical Director [[Gianluca Nani]], had part financed the deal to buy Franco from their own salaries.<ref>[http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/standard-sport/football/article-23748826-west-ham-chiefs-pay-for-striker-with-their-own-money.do West Ham chiefs pay for striker with their own money] www.thisislondon.co.uk </ref>
He made his debut for West Ham on 17 October 2009 in a 2-1 away defeat to [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]].<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8305444.stm Stoke 2 - 1 West Ham]</ref>
He scored his first goal for West Ham on 31 October 2009 to put them 1-0 up against [[Sunderland F.C.|Sunderland]] away from home in a game which finished 2-2.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8328814.stm Sunderland 2 - 2 West Ham]</ref> Franco became the third Mexican player to score a league goal in the [[Premier League]], [[Jared Borgetti]] and [[Carlos Vela]] being the first and second respectively.{{Citation needed|date=November 2009}}

== International Career ==
In 2004 Franco became a [[naturalized]] Mexican citizen<ref>[http://www.guardian.co.uk/football/2009/sep/17/guillermo-franco-transfer-west-ham-football Guillermo Franco signs for West Ham] www.guardian.co.uk</ref> after settling in Mexico in 2002 and made his debut for the national side in 2005. Guillermo Luis Franco Farcuason, commonly known as Guille Franco, was born on November 3, 1976, in Corrientes, Argentina. He is an Argentinian-born Mexican football player who has played as a striker throughout his career. Franco's journey in football began in his home country before he moved to Mexico and eventually to Europe.

## Career Overview

### Early Career in Argentina

Franco started his professional career with San Lorenzo, an Argentine first division club, where he played from 1996 to 2002. During this period, he made 96 appearances and scored 23 goals for the club. This experience laid the foundation for his future success in other leagues.

### Success in Mexico

In 2002, Franco transferred to Monterrey, a prominent club in the Mexican league. His time with Monterrey was highly successful, spanning from 2002 to 2005. He made 119 appearances and scored 63 goals, leading the league in scoring during the 2004 Apertura with 15 goals in 16 games. Additionally, he was part of the team that won the championship in 2003 and finished as runners-up in 2004 and 2005.

### European Experience

Franco then moved to Spain, joining Villarreal CF in 2006. Despite facing injury issues, he managed to contribute significantly, scoring 14 goals in 81 appearances over three years. One notable achievement was scoring the winning goal against Celta Vigo, which helped Villarreal qualify for the UEFA Cup.

### Premier League Debut

In September 2009, Franco signed with West Ham United, becoming the first Mexican player to join the club. Due to West Ham's financial difficulties, the deal was partly financed by the club's CEO, Scott Duxbury, and their Sporting and Football Technical Director, Gianluca Nani, using their own salaries. Franco made his debut for West Ham on October 17, 2009, and scored his first goal for the club on October 31, 2009, against Sunderland. The league's top four teams qualify for UEFA competitions. '''Javier Alejandro Mascherano''' ({{IPA-it|maskeˈɾano}}; born 8 June 1984 in [[San Lorenzo, Santa Fe|San Lorenzo]]) is an [[Argentina|Argentine]] [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]] for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Captain (association football)|captains]] the [[Argentina national football team|Argentine national team]].

Mascherano began his career in at [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]]. He earned his first senior honours in 2003–04,  winning the [[Primera División Argentina]]. He also won an [[Argentina at the 2004 Summer Olympics|Olympic gold medal]] with Argentina in the [[2004 Summer Olympics|Athens Games]] and finished runner up in the [[Copa América 2004]]. He moved to Brazilian side [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] in 2005, winning the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Brazilian Série A]] in his first season. Mascherano moved to Europe, signing for [[Premier League]] side [[West Ham United]]. However, unusual contract terms with [[Media Sports Investments]] blighted his brief time at the club and at the beginning of 2007 he joined [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on loan.

He was runner up in the [[UEFA Champions League]] in his first season on [[Merseyside]] and again finished runner up in the Copa América with Argentina. He officially signed for Liverpool in February 2008 for £18.6 million, parting ways with Media Sports Investments. He won a second Olympic gold medal with Argentina in the [[2008 Summer Olympics|Beijing 2008 Games]], the first male footballer to achieve this since 1928. He was appointed captain of the national team by new head coach [[Diego Maradona]] in November 2008 whom has repeatedly stated  that his ''Seleccion'' is Mascherano and 10 more.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/maradona-argentina-mascherano/dasftb/20090306dasdasftb_58/Tes |title=Maradona: "Argentina son Mascherano y diez más" |publisher=''as.com'' {{es icon}} |accessdate=2009-03-29 }}</ref>

Mascherano's two most used nicknames (in Argentina) are ''Masche'' and ''El Jefecito'' (The little chief).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clarin.com/diario/2006/04/23/deportes/d-06601.htm |title=Tevez-Mascherano: "Enfrentar a River, para nosotros es algo distinto" |publisher=''[[Clarín (newspaper)|Clarín]]'' {{es icon}} |accessdate=2007-04-28 }}</ref><ref name=skysports>{{cite web |title=Player profile - Javier Mascherano |publisher=SkySports.com |url=http://home.skysports.com/worldcup/player.aspx?plid=40672&clid=632 |accessdate=2007-03-04 }}</ref> Former Argentine footballers [[Jorge Valdano]] and [[Jorge Solari]] regard him as possibly the best central midfielder in the world.<ref name=BBC>{{cite web |title= Valdano on Maradona, Mascherano et al. |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/7690933.stm |accessdate=2008-10-04 }}</ref><ref name=Soccernet>{{cite web |title= Solari heaps praise on Argentina's Mascherano |publisher=[[ESPN Soccernet]] |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=654565&sec=worldcup2010&cc=5739 |accessdate=2009-06-13 }}</ref>

==Club career==
===River Plate (2003–05)===
Mascherano came through the youth ranks at [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] in [[Buenos Aires]], [[Argentina]]. However, before making his club debut he made his name representing Argentina.

Mascherano won his first silverware when River won the [[2003-2004 in Argentine football|2003–04 Clausura (Closing) championship]]. In the 2004 [[Copa Libertadores]] River reached the semi-final, but lost on penalties to arch-rivals [[Club Atlético Boca Juniors|Boca Juniors]].

Around this time several clubs including [[Real Madrid]],<ref name=Alonso> {{cite web |last=Northcroft |first=Johnathon |title=Mascherano happy to step out of the shadows |work=[[The Times]] |date=2007-04-08 |url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/article1626232.ece |accessdate=2008-11-13}} </ref> and [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] declared an interest in signing Mascherano, but River Plate turned down all offers, saying that none of the interested parties were prepared to pay enough.

2004–05 was not a successful season for River, finishing third in the Apertura Championship and only tenth in the Clausura. In the Copa Libertadores River again lost in the semi-final, this time to [[São Paulo Futebol Clube|São Paulo]].

After the [[2005 FIFA Confederations Cup|Confederations Cup]] in Germany, Brazilian club [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] acquired Mascherano from River Plate for US$15 million.

===Corinthians (2005–06)===
The Brazilian Série A runs from April, so Mascherano joined [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] in mid-season. After playing only nine games for his new club, on September 2005, Mascherano suffered a stress fracture to his left foot causing him to miss the end of the season. He went back to Argentina to be operated on by the National team doctor and recuperate.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://fifaworldcup.yahoo.com/06/en/050928/1/4rtc.html |title=Injury jinx hits Argentina |work=FIFAWorldCup.yahoo.com |date=2005-09-28 |accessdate=2007-03-15 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clarin.com/diario/2005/12/30/deportes/d-01116361.htm |title=Argentine players injured |work=[[Clarín (newspaper)|Clarín]] |accessdate=2007-03-15}}  {{es icon}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://globoesporte.

### Biography of Javier Mascherano

Javier Alejandro Mascherano, born on June 8, 1984, in San Lorenzo, Argentina, is a renowned Argentine footballer who primarily plays as a defensive midfielder. Standing at 5 feet 7 inches tall, Mascherano has had a significant impact on both club and international levels throughout his career. He currently plays for Liverpool F.C., wearing the number 20 jersey, and serves as the captain of the Argentine national team. [Data: Infobox Football biography 2 (1)]

#### Early Career and Youth Development

Mascherano began his professional journey at Club Atlético River Plate, where he quickly established himself as a key player. During his tenure at River Plate from 2003 to 2005, he helped the team win the Primera División Argentina in the 2003-2004 Clausura championship. His performances also earned him a place in the Argentina U-20 team, where he played in the 2003 FIFA Under-20 World Cup. Additionally, he represented Argentina in the 2004 Athens Olympics, contributing to the team's gold medal victory. [Data: Infobox Football biography 2 (1)]

#### Move to Brazil and Europe

In 2005, Mascherano transferred to Sport Club Corinthians Paulista in Brazil, where he won the Campeonato Brasileiro Série A in his first season. However, his time at Corinthians was cut short due to a stress fracture in his left foot, which required surgery and rehabilitation. This injury marked the beginning of his European adventure, as he moved to West Ham United in the Premier League in 2006. Despite facing contractual issues with Media Sports Investments, Mascherano managed to secure a loan move to Liverpool F.C. in early 2007. [Data: Infobox Football biography 2 (1)]

#### Success at Liverpool F.C.

At Liverpool, Mascherano became a pivotal figure in the midfield, helping the team reach the UEFA Champions League final in his first season. He officially joined Liverpool in February 2008 for £18.6 million, marking the end of his association with Media Sports Investments. With Liverpool, Mascherano continued to excel, earning recognition for his defensive prowess and leadership qualities. [Data: Infobox Football biography 2 (1)]

#### International Career

On the international stage, Mascherano has been a consistent presence for the Argentine national team since 2003. He has accumulated over 55 caps and scored two goals for his country. Under the guidance of former head coach Diego Maradona, Mascherano was appointed as the captain of the national team in November 2008. Maradona famously stated that his team was "Mascherano and ten more," highlighting the player's importance to the squad. [Data: Infobox Football biography 2 (1)]

#### Achievements and Recognition

Throughout his career, Mascherano has achieved numerous accolades, including two Olympic gold medals in 2004 and 2008. He is also regarded as one of the best central midfielders in the world by former Argentine footballers Jorge Valdano and Jorge Solari. His contributions have earned him the nicknames "Masche" and "El Jefecito" (The little chief) among fans and teammates alike. [Data: Infobox Football biography 2 (1)]

In summary, Javier Mascherano's career is marked by success and leadership, both at the club and international levels. His journey from River Plate to Liverpool, and his role as the captain of the Argentine national team, exemplify his enduring impact on the sport of football.

## Overview of FK Inkaras Kaunas

FK Inkaras Kaunas is a Lithuanian football team based in the city of Kaunas. The club was founded in 1937 and dissolved in 2003. Despite its relatively short lifespan, FK Inkaras achieved significant success during its existence, winning seven Lithuanian Championships and seven Lithuanian Cups. Additionally, the club won one Lithuanian Supercup in 1995. [Data: Achievements (1937-2003)]

## Season-by-Season Performance

### Early Years (1991-1994)
From 1991 to 1994, FK Inkaras struggled to maintain a consistent position in the top division. They finished 14th in 1991, 10th in 1991/92, 9th in 1992/93, and 8th in 1993/94. During this period, the club's performance was marked by a high number of losses and a relatively low goal difference. [Data: Season-by-season (1991-1994)]

### Golden Era (1994-1996)
The club's fortunes changed dramatically starting in 1994/95 when they clinched the championship with a dominant performance, finishing first with 32 points and a goal difference of 50-12. This success was followed by another championship win in 1995/96, where they amassed an impressive 56 points and a goal difference of 67-9. [Data: Season-by-season (1994-1996)]

### Later Years (1996-2002)
After the golden years, FK Inkaras continued to perform well but did not repeat the same level of dominance. They finished third in 1996/97, fourth in 1997/98, and fifth in both 1998/99 and 2001. The club also participated in European competitions, including the UEFA Cup and Intertoto Cup, though they were unable to advance beyond the preliminary rounds or first qualifying rounds. [Data: Season-by-season (1996-2002); European cup history (1995-1999)]

## Conclusion

Despite its dissolution in 2003, FK Inkaras Kaunas left a lasting legacy in Lithuanian football. The club's achievements, particularly its multiple championships and cups, highlight its significance in the country's football history. [Data: Achievements (1937-2003)]

'''FSV Frankfurt''' is a [[Germany|German]] [[football (soccer)|football]] [[List of football clubs in Germany|club]] based in the Bornheim district of [[Frankfurt]], [[Hesse]] and founded in 1899. The club plays in the shadow of larger and much more successful ''[[Eintracht Frankfurt]]'', but has recently returned to 2<sup>nd</sup> tier football. FSV Frankfurt also fielded a highly successful women's team, which was disbanded in 2006.

==History==
The club was one of the founding members of the ''[[Nordkreis-Liga]]'' in 1909, when football started to become more organised in Southern Germany. With the outbreak of the [[First World War]] in 1914, this league came to a halt but a championship for the region was still held, which ''FSV'' won in 1917.<ref>''Süddeutschlands Fussball in Tabellenform 1897 - 1988'', {{de icon}} author: Ludolf Hyll, page: 32-55, accessed: 20 April 2009</ref>

After the war, the club became part of the [[Kreisliga Nordmain]], which it managed to win in 1922-23, advancing to the [[Southern German championship]], where it finished last out of five teams.<ref>''Süddeutschlands Fussball in Tabellenform 1897 - 1988'', {{de icon}} author: Ludolf Hyll, page: 72-74, accessed: 20 April 2009</ref>

The pinnacle of the team's achievement was a losing appearance in the 1925 national final, 0:1 to [[1. FC Nuremberg]], and the capture of a German amateur title in 1972 in a 2:1 victory over ''[[Marl Hüls]]''. The club contested the 1938 Tschammerpokal final, predecessor of today's [[German Cup]], and were beaten 1:3 by ''[[Rapid Vienna]]''.

The club played in the ''[[Bezirksliga Main]]'', then the ''[[Bezirksliga Main-Hessen]]'' throughout the 1920s and 30's. After capturing the championship of the VSFV (Verband Süddeutscher Fussball Vereine or Federation of South German Football Clubs) in 1933, ''FSV'' went on to play in the ''[[Gauliga Südwest]]'', one of sixteen top-flight divisions formed that same year in the re-organization of German football under the [[Third Reich]]. They consistently earned mid-table results there with the club's best finish being a second place in 1939. In 1941 the Gauliga Hessen was split into the Gauliga Westmark and the Gauliga Hessen-Nassau with ''FSV'' playing in the latter division. The team finished a close second to ''[[Kickers Offenbach]]'' in 1943 and in 1944 merged briefly with ''SG Eintracht Frankfurt'' to play as the wartime side (Kriegspielgemeinschaft) ''KSG Frankfurt''. The following season the Gauliga collapsed with the advance of Allied armies into Germany as [[World War II]] drew to a close.

After the war occupying Allied authorities order the dissolution of all organizations in Germany, including sports and football clubs. ''Frankfurt'' was re-established as ''SG Bornheim'' but had taken on their old identity again by late 1945. The team resumed play in the first division [[Oberliga Süd (1945-63)|Oberliga Süd]] where they played undistinguished, middling football until relegated at the end of the 1961-62 season. The [[Bundesliga (football)|Bundesliga]], Germany's first top-flight professional league, was formed in 1963. ''FSV'' joined the [[Regionalliga Süd (1963-74)|Regionalliga Süd]] and remained a regular tier II side from the early 60's through to the early 70s when they slipped to third division play. The club returned to the second tier in 1975 a year after the formation of the 2.Bundesliga, playing in the [[2nd Bundesliga Süd (1974-81)|2nd Bundesliga Süd]]. In 1981 the northern and southern divisions of this league were combined and as a perennial lower table side ''FSV'' was delivered to the third division [[Oberliga Hessen]] (III). The club made a single season cameo appearance in the combined league in 1982-83 before once again falling back.

They played in the Regionalliga Süd (III) in 2007-08 after seven seasons in the Amateur Oberliga Hessen (IV). Winning the championship of the Regionalliga Süd (III), the club has been promoted to the [[2. Fußball-Bundesliga|2nd Bundesliga]] for the season 2008-2009.

He had a successful return to Lorient for the [[Ligue 1 season 2006-07|2006–07 Ligue 1 season]] appearing in 37 matches and scoring 9 goals to become their leading goalscorer, including a [[Hat-trick#Association_football|hat trick]] in 27 minutes in the opening match of the season against [[Derby Breton|Bretagne rivals]] [[FC Nantes|Nantes]].

At the end of the season, on 25 June 2007, it was announced that Gignac had signed a four-year deal with [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]].<ref>[http://www.football365.fr/la-une/article_172435_Toulouse-Gignac-arrive.shtml]</ref> However, it was revealed soon after that Lorient had accepted a [[€]]4.5m bid from [[Lille OSC]] and that the player had already agreed to a pre-contract with the Northern side,  putting his move to Toulouse in jeopardy.<ref>[http://www.mercato365.com/article_172721_L-imbroglio-Gignac.shtml L’IMBROGLIO GIGNAC]</ref> Despite this, Toulouse trumped Lille's offer by offering the player more than double the salary he had been offered by Lille.<ref name="L’imbroglio Gignac">[http://www.mercato365.com/article_172721_L-imbroglio-Gignac.shtml L’imbroglio Gignac]</ref> The clubs entered a war of words with Toulouse questioning the legitimacy of Lille's agreement while Gignac and Lille questioned the ethics and tactics of Toulouse.<ref name="L’imbroglio Gignac"/> Eventually, Gignac's move to Toulouse was validated.

Gignac made his competitive debut for Toulouse in the first leg of their [[UEFA Champions League]] third qualifying round match against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], coming on as a substitute in the 65th minute. Toulouse lost the match 0–1 and eventually lost the two-legged tie 0–5 on aggregate, thus being eliminated from the Champions League. Despite the hype, both Gignac and Toulouse had disappointing [[Ligue 1 2007-08|07–08 seasons]] with Gignac appearing in 28 matches and scoring only two goals. Toulouse finished the season in 17th place, just one place above the relegation zone. Some attributed Gignac's struggle for form to him playing second fiddle to [[Sweden|Swedish]] striker [[Johan Elmander]].<ref name="guardian.co.uk">[http://www.guardian.co.uk/football/blog/2009/mar/24/ben-lyttleton-ligue-gignac-toulouse Gignac's rocky road takes a turn for the better with call for national service]</ref>

On 4 October 2007, after coming on as a substitute for Elmander, Gignac scored a [[last-minute goal]] against [[Bulgaria]]n side [[PFC CSKA Sofia|CSKA Sofia]] to cancel out [[Claudinei Alexandre Aparecido]]'s opening goal from the penalty spot and enable his team to progress to the group stages of the [[UEFA Cup 2007–08|UEFA Cup]] on the [[away goals rule]].<ref>[https://www.euro2008.com/competitions/uefacup/fixturesresults/round=15118/match=301475/report=lu.html]</ref>

His debut for the Blues came under manager [[Miroslav Blažević]] in the first match of the season, a [[Prva HNL]] away game against against [[NK Varteks|Varteks]] on 23 August 1992, which made him the youngest ever player to debut for the club as Šimić was only three months shy from his 17th birthday. He continued to make five more appearances in his first top-flight season and although was widely regarded as a promising player, he struggled to make a bigger impact in his first season with the squad which eventually won the Croatian title that year.

However, right from the beginning of the [[1993–94 Prva HNL|1993–94 season]] he established himself as a first team regular and was one of the key players of the squad in one of the most successful periods in club's history. In the next six seasons Šimić helped the club win another four titles as well as four [[Croatian Cup]]s. In this period Šimić also experienced his first taste of European football when Dinamo (known as ''Croatia Zagreb'' from 1992 to 2000) played [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]] in a [[1994–95 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|1994–95 Cup Winners' Cup]] first round tie as he appeared a 3–1 home win at [[Stadion Maksimir|Maksimir]] on 29 September 1994. He regularly appeared in all of the club's European campaigns over the following four seasons and took part in some of the club's biggest achievements in recent times, such as reaching the [[1997–98 UEFA Cup]] round of 16 (where they were knocked out by [[Atlético Madrid]] 2–1 on aggregate) and group stage of the [[1998–99 UEFA Champions League|1998–99 Champions League]] (after knocking out [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] 3–1 on aggregate in the second qualifying round).

Other notable Dinamo players and Šimić's teammates from that era were [[Silvio Marić]], [[Dražen Ladić]], [[Igor Cvitanović]], [[Mark Viduka]] and [[Robert Prosinečki]], as well as [[Krunoslav Jurčić]] and [[Goran Jurić]] with whom he formed a solid defensive partnership. In his six and a half years with the club, Šimić earned a total of 140 league appearances and scored 14 goals.

In the meantime Šimić's former coach at Dinamo, Miroslav Blažević, was appointed [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] manager in 1994. In 1996, impressed by his string of good performances, Blažević called him up and, after playing 16 games for Croatia's youth teams, Šimić earned his first full international cap on 13 March 1996 in a friendly against South Korea, coming on as a substitute for [[Igor Štimac]]. Šimić quickly became a first team regular in the national team under Blažević, and went on to play in six [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] qualifiers, as well as six matches at the final tournament itself in [[France]], where Croatia eventually won third place.

== Narendra Man Singh ==
 

Narendra Man Singh born on kathmandu, nepal was a great player of his time.. He was given the title "greatest striker and a play maker". He have a wife and a son. He turned out to be a great husband and  a father too.

A year later, he played in the national jersey in the ninth Asian Games in New Delhi in 1982.

He is the first Nepali player to play the professional football in India. He started from Mafatlal Group SC, Mumbai, and later shifted to Mahindra & Mahindra, now known as Mahindra United, the first division club of Indian League.

Singh spent eight years in the Indian football and returned in 1990 to join Sankata in the Martyrs Memorial league in 1995, 1997 and 2000. He also assumed roles of vice-president and coach for Sankata.

Before starting his professional football life in India, he played for Sankata, RCT, Royal Drugs, Friends Club and Nepal Army Club.

'''Blackburn Rovers Football Club''' ({{pron-en|ˈblækbərn ˈroʊvər}}) is an English [[FA Premier League|Premier League]] [[Association football|football]] club based in the town of [[Blackburn]], [[Lancashire]]. 

The club was established in 1875, becoming a founding member of [[The Football League]] in 1888. It is one of only three clubs to have been both a founder member of the Football League and the Premier League (the others being [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] and [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]). In 1890 Rovers moved to its permanent home at [[Ewood Park]]. Prior to the formation of the [[FA Premier League|Premier League]] in 1992, most of the club's successes were before 1930, when it had gained league and [[FA Cup]] trophies on several occasions. Relegation in 1966 was followed by 26 successive seasons of football outside the top flight.

In 1992, Blackburn were promoted to the new Premier League a year after being taken over by local [[Business magnate|steel baron]] [[Jack Walker]], who installed [[Kenny Dalglish]] as manager. In 1995, Blackburn became league champions, having spent millions of pounds on players like [[Alan Shearer]] and [[Chris Sutton]]. However, the title-winning team was quickly split up and, in 1999, the club were relegated. They were promoted back to the Premiership two years later, just after Walker's death, and have been in the top flight ever since. During this time they have qualified for the UEFA Cup four times: once as League Cup winners, twice as the Premiership's sixth-placed team and once via the [[Intertoto Cup]].

The club's [[Latin]] motto ''"Arte et labore"'', the club's translation of this is "By Skill & Hard Work".

== History ==
{{recentism|date=June 2008}}
{{main|History of Blackburn Rovers F.C.}}
=== The early years ===
The club Blackburn Rovers was the idea of [[John Lewis (referee)|John Lewis]] and Arthur Constantine during a seventeen-man meeting at the [[Leger Hotel]], Blackburn on the 5 November 1875. The club's first secretary was Walter Duckworth, and Lewis was its first treasurer. Many of the initial members were wealthy and well-connected, and this helped the club survive and rise beyond the large number of other local teams around at the time. [[Blackburn]] has had a particular strong history of football, Rovers were not the town's only side in the 19th century; other rivals included [[Blackburn Olympic F.C.]] (1883 winners of the [[FA Cup]]) and [[Blackburn Park Road F.C.]], among others.

[[Image:Leaflet advert for blackburn rovers match-1887.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Leaflet advertising a Blackburn Rovers match on the 12 September 1887 against '[[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|The Wednesday]]' at [[Olive Grove]].]]

The first match played by Blackburn Rovers took place in [[Church, Lancashire]] on 18 December 1875 and was a 1–1 draw. Although the make-up of the team was not recorded it is generally thought to be: Thomas Greenwood (goal), Jack Baldwin, Fred Birtwistle, (full-backs), Arthur Thomas, J. T. Sycelmore (half-backs), Walter Duckworth, [[John Lewis (referee)|John Lewis]], Thomas Dean, Arthur Constantine, Harry Greenwood, Ed Youngson (forwards), in a 2-2-6 formation.

At the time, the club had no ground of its own and no gate receipts. The only income came from members' subscriptions, which totalled £2 8s 0d during the first season.

During the [[1876-77 in English football|1876–77]] season, Rovers finally gained a ground of its own by renting  a piece of farmland at [[Oozehead]], on the west side of town facing Preston New Road. The ground was little more than a meadow with a pool in the middle that had to be covered with planks and turf for matches. But it did allow the club to collect gate receipts totalling 6s 6d for the season. Occasional games were also played at [[Pleasington Cricket Ground]].

Subsequently Blackburn Rovers rented [[Alexandra Meadows]], the home of the East Lancashire Cricket Club, for their matches. The inaugural game at Alexandra Meadows was played against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], the most prestigious club Rovers had played until then. The result was a 2–1 win for Blackburn, with two goals from Richard Birtwistle.

On 28 September 1878, Blackburn Rovers became one of 23 clubs to form the Lancashire Football Association. On 1 November, 1879 the club played in the F.A. Cup for the first time, beating the Tyne Association Football Club 5–1. Rovers were eventually put out of the competition in the third round after suffering a heavy 6–0 defeat by [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]]. 

Controversy erupted during 1880 when the club used players not from Blackburn to fill in for unavailable team members—this violated what, at the time, was considered an important principle of the LFA. The situation became worse at the start of the 1881 season when a [[Darwen F.C.|Darwen]] player transferred to Blackburn Rovers. The move caused a great deal of bitterness between the clubs and local populations. Accusations of professionalism began to fly, with Darwen accusing Blackburn Rovers of offering the player in question, [[Fergie Suter]], improved terms. However, Suter had initially moved to Darwen from Scotland and given up his trade as [[stonemason]] to play for the club. So the professional/amateur divide was already blurred. Nevertheless, subsequent matches between Blackburn Rovers and Darwen were fractious affairs both on and off the pitch. The teams were drawn against each other in the fourth round of the Lancashire Cup, and the clubs refused to agree on a date for the match. As a result the LFA ejected both teams from the competition. This type of controversy would only be resolved five years later in 1885 with the legalisation of professionalism.

During the [[1881-82 in English football|1881–82]] season, the club continued to rent the facilities at Alexandra Meadows, but began to look towards a move elsewhere. A ground was leased at [[Leamington Street]] and £500 was spent on a new grandstand capable of seating 600 to 700 spectators. ### Overview of Blackburn Rovers Football Club

Blackburn Rovers Football Club (often referred to as "Rovers," "Blue and Whites," or "The Riversiders") is an English Premier League football club based in Blackburn, Lancashire. Established in 1875, the club has a rich history and has been a part of significant milestones in English football. The club's Latin motto, "Arte et labore," translates to "By Skill & Hard Work." Over the years, Blackburn Rovers have achieved notable success, including winning the Premier League championship in 1995 under the management of Kenny Dalglish. The club plays its home games at Ewood Park, which has a capacity of 31,367 spectators. The current manager is Sam Allardyce, and Ryan Nelsen serves as the captain.

### Historical Background

#### Early Years

The club was founded on November 5, 1875, following a meeting at the Leger Hotel in Blackburn. Initially, the club faced financial challenges due to the lack of a dedicated ground and gate receipts. The first match was played on December 18, 1875, resulting in a 1–1 draw. Over the next few years, Blackburn Rovers secured a ground at Oozehead, which allowed them to collect gate receipts. The club's first significant achievement came in 1879 when they entered the FA Cup for the first time, defeating the Tyne Association Football Club 5–1. However, they were eliminated in the third round by Nottingham Forest.

#### Controversies and Professionalism

In 1880, controversy arose when Blackburn Rovers used non-local players, violating the principles of the Lancashire Football Association (LFA). This issue escalated in 1881 when a player from Darwen, Fergie Suter, transferred to Blackburn Rovers. This move led to bitter rivalries and accusations of professionalism. Matches between the two clubs became contentious, and both were eventually expelled from the Lancashire Cup competition. These controversies were eventually resolved in 1885 with the legalization of professionalism in English football.

#### Moving to Leamington Street

During the 1881–82 season, Blackburn Rovers continued to use the facilities at Alexandra Meadows but began planning a move to a new ground. They leased a site at Leamington Street and invested £500 in constructing a grandstand that could seat 600 to 700 spectators. This move was seen as necessary for the club to establish itself as a leading force in the region. The club also implemented measures such as boards around the pitch to prevent crowd disturbances and erected an ornate entrance arch bearing the club's name.

### Modern Era

#### Premier League Success

Blackburn Rovers joined the Premier League in 1992, a year after being taken over by local steel magnate Jack Walker. Under the management of Kenny Dalglish, the club achieved significant success, winning the Premier League championship in 1995. This victory was made possible by substantial investments in players like Alan Shearer and Chris Sutton. However, the success was short-lived, and the club was relegated in 1999. They returned to the Premier League in 2001, shortly after Jack Walker's death, and have remained in the top flight since then.

#### European Competitions

Since returning to the Premier League, Blackburn Rovers have qualified for the UEFA Cup on four occasions. They achieved this through various means, including winning the League Cup, finishing sixth in the Premier League, and qualifying via the Intertoto Cup. These European campaigns have added to the club's international profile and provided valuable experience for the players.

### Current Status

As of the 2008–09 season, Blackburn Rovers were competing in the Premier League, finishing in 15th position. The club continues to be managed by Sam Allardyce, with Neil McDonald serving as the assistant manager. The ownership structure remains unique, with the club being owned by the Trustees of the Jack Walker 1987 Settlement, a Jersey trust. John Williams holds the position of chairman, overseeing the club's operations and strategic direction.

Overall, Blackburn Rovers Football Club has a storied history marked by periods of success and challenges. Their journey from a small club in the late 19th century to a prominent figure in modern English football is a testament to their resilience and determination.

He became a regular in the Under-17 side during the 2002–03 season, and picked up an [[FA Youth Cup]] winner's medal despite playing second fiddle to [[Luke Steele (footballer)|Luke Steele]] throughout the entire competition. He made his first appearance in the reserve team the following season, starting in a 3–1 home win over [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] in the Premier Reserve League on 2 October 2003. At the end of the 2003–04 season, Heaton was named on the bench for the final of the [[Manchester Senior Cup]] against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], and won a winner's medal despite not taking the field. By the 2004–05 season, Heaton had become the first-choice goalkeeper for the Manchester United reserve team, and was named on the bench for the first team for [[Stan Ternent]]'s testimonial on 17 August 2004, coming on as a 76th-minute substitute for [[Luke Steele (footballer)|Luke Steele]] after Steele had earlier come on for [[Tim Howard]]. With Heaton in goal for 17 of the 28 [[Premier Reserve League]] North matches and 12 of the 22 [[Central League (football)|Central League]] matches, the team went on to win both league titles by nine and five points respectively. Heaton's form for the reserves resulted in him being loaned out to [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] at the start of the [[2005-06 in English football|2005–06]], initially until 1 January 2006. During his time at Swindon, he played over 20 games, saving a penalty on his debut, and was described as "one for the future" by manager [[Iffy Onuora]]. He returned to Manchester United, but, after the recall of [[Ritchie Jones]] from [[Royal Antwerp FC|Royal Antwerp]], Heaton was sent there for the rest of the season after United rebuffed an approach from [[Huddersfield Town F.C.|Huddersfield Town]]. Heaton made his second appearance for the Manchester United first team on 13 March 2007, coming on as a half-time substitute for [[Tomasz Kuszczak]] in the [[UEFA Celebration Match]] against [[Marcello Lippi]]'s Europe XI. Heaton spent the [[2007-08 in English football|2007–08]] season with the first team squad at Manchester United, appearing on the bench when [[Edwin van der Sar]] was out due to injury. ===Cardiff City loan=== At the end of the 2007–08 season, Heaton agreed to move to [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] on loan for the duration of the [[2008-09 in English football|2008-09 season]].{{cite news |title=Cardiff sign Man Utd goalkeeper |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/c/cardiff_city/7407805.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=[[2008-05-23]] |accessdate=2008-05-23 }} He was chosen as the club's first choice goalkeeper, above [[Finland national football team|Finland]] international [[Peter Enckelman]], for the start of the season by manager [[Dave Jones]],{{cite news |first=Terry |last=Phillips |title=Heaton wins Bluebirds keeper battle for Saints start |url=http://www.walesonline.co.uk/footballnation/cardiff-city-fc/2008/08/08/heaton-wins-bluebirds-keeper-battle-for-saints-start-91466-21490131/ |work=[[Western Mail]] |publisher=Media Wales |date=8 August 2008 |accessdate=29 August 2008 }} and played in every match until late November, with the exception of the [[Football League Cup|Carling Cup]] third round tie against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]], when he was replaced by Enckelman.{{cite news |title=Swansea 1-0 Cardiff |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/league_cup/7626773.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=23 September 2008 |accessdate=18 February 2009 }} However, late on in Cardiff's 2–1 away defeat to [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] on 22 November 2008, Heaton picked up an injury and was forced off. The injury would go on to cost Heaton his place in the side as the club went unbeaten with Enckelman in goal for over two months. In February, Enckelman was forced to undergo knee surgery which saw Heaton return in goal on 16 February 2009, when he picked up the [[man of the match]] award in a 4-0 defeat at the hands of [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. However, he tore his thigh muscle during the match, ruling him out for up to five weeks.{{cite news |title=Cardiff rocked by keeper injury |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/c/cardiff_city/7895288.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 February 2009 |accessdate=18 February 2009 }} On his return, Heaton found himself on the bench behind loanee [[Stuart Taylor (footballer born 1980)|Stuart Taylor]] but, following a 6-0 defeat against [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]], he replaced Taylor for the final three matches of the season. However, he was unable to keep Cardiff in the play-off places and he returned to Manchester United at the end of the season.[http://www.walesonline.co.uk/footballnation/cardiff-city-fc/2009/05/16/cardiff-city-set-to-offer-skipper-s-armband-to-roger-johnson-91466-23635559/ "Cardiff City set to offer skipper's armband to Roger Johnson"] [[South Wales Echo]] Retrieved on 15 May, 2009 ===Queens Park Rangers loan=== On 15 August 2009, Heaton was signed by [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] on an emergency three-month loan deal, the terms of which will allow him to compete in the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]].{{cite news |title=Exclusive: United Keeper Pens Loan |url=http://www.qpr.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10373~1754286,00.html |work=qpr.co.uk |publisher=Queens Park Rangers FC |date=15 August 2009 |accessdate=15 August 2009 }} Heaton's loan spell ended on 8 November 2009. ===Rochdale loan=== After returning from [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]], Heaton joined [[Rochdale F.C.|Rochdale]] on 13 Novemb

### Coventry City

'''Walsall Football Club''' ({{pron-en|ˈwɔlsɔl}}) are an English [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Walsall]], [[West Midlands (region)|West Midlands]]. They currently play in [[Football League One|League One]]. The club was founded in 1888 as '''Walsall Town Swifts''', an amalgamation of '''Walsall Town F.C.''' and '''Walsall Swifts F.C.''' The club were one of the founder members of the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] in 1892, but have spent their entire existence outside of English football's top division; their highest league finish was sixth in Division Two in [[1898–99 in English football|1898–99]].

Walsall moved into their [[Bescot Stadium]] in 1990, having previously played at nearby [[Fellows Park]]. Their opening game was a friendly fixture against local rivals [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], with Villa winning 4–0. The ground is now known as Banks's Stadium for sponsorship purposes.<ref name="Walsall rename ground Banks's Stadium">{{cite news
| title = Walsall rename ground Banks's Stadium
| url = http://www.football-shirts.co.uk/fans/125
| publisher = Football Shirts
| date = 11 May 2007
| accessdate =11 May 2007}}</ref> The team play in a red and white kit and their club crest features a [[swift]]. They have rivalries with neighbouring [[Black Country]] teams, [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] (though these teams are often more concerned with their rivalry against each other, rather than against Walsall), with more 'reciprocal' rivalries against [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] and [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]]. The club's nickname, '''''The Saddlers''''', reflects Walsall's status as a traditional centre for [[saddle]] manufacture.

==History==
{{recentism|date=August 2009}}
{{see also|Walsall F.C. seasons}}
[[Image:WalsallFC1893.jpg|thumb|right|The Walsall team pictured in 1893]]
Walsall were formed as '''Walsall Town Swifts''' in 1888 when '''Walsall Town F.C.''' and '''Walsall Swifts F.C.''' amalgamated. Walsall Town had been founded in 1877 and Walsall Swifts in 1879. Walsall Town Swifts' first match was a draw against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]. In 1889 Town Swifts' first England international, [[Albert Aldridge]] was capped twice by his country. The club were first admitted to the [[The Football League|Football League]] in 1892, as founder members of the new [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]], but in 1894–95 finished 14th out of 16 teams and failed to be re-elected to the Football League. They changed their name to Walsall F.C. and joined the Midland League.

Walsall's highest "home" attendance was set in 1930, when they played in of front of 74,600 fans against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in the [[FA Cup]] Fourth Round. Although a home match for Walsall, the tie was played at their opponents' [[Villa Park]] ground, and it remains the highest attendance that Walsall have ever played in front of. Walsall was a founding member of the [[Football League Third Division North|Third Division North]] in 1921. In 1933 won 2–0 in the [[FA Cup]] against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], who went on to win the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] that season.

In 1958, following a reorganisation of the Football League, Walsall became founder members of the Fourth Division. Under the management of Bill Moore, the club achieved successive promotions, scoring 102 goals on their way to winning Division Four in 1959–60 and finishing as Division Three runners-up in 1960–61 to reach the second tier of English football for the first time since the early 1900s. Players such as Bill 'Chopper' Guttridge, Tony Richards and Colin Taylor were intrinsically important to the success of the side. After just two seasons in the Second Division, the club were relegated back to Division Three in 1962–63, and remained there until a further demotion to the Fourth Division, in 1978–79.

The club has always had a rich history of producing players who go on to play at the top level. [[Allan Clarke (footballer)|Allan Clarke]] went on to win the [[English football champions|League Championship]] under Don Revie at [[Leeds United]] after beginning life at Fellows Park. [[Bert Williams]] and [[Phil Parkes (footballer born 1950)|Phil Parkes]] both became England Goalkeepers in the years after they progressed from their roots in Walsall. [[David Kelly (footballer)|David Kelly]] had a long career at the top level after leaving Walsall in 1988, representing the Republic of Ireland at the very highest level of international football. More recently, [[Michael Ricketts]] represented England after blossoming at Bolton Wanderers. In recent years, [[Matty Fryatt]] and Ishmel Demontagnac have both represented England age-groups.

The 1980s were a period of considerable activity for Walsall. In 1983–84 they defeated First Division club Arsenal in [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] play, and advanced to the semi-final, where they gained a 2–2 draw against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[Anfield]], but lost the second leg 2–0 and the tie 4–2 on aggregate. Walsall narrowly missed out on promotion in the same season.

In 1986 plans were announced to move Walsall to Birmingham, to [[groundshare]] with [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]]. The town rallied behind Barrie Blower, who led a campaign to save the club. Walsall were subsequently bought by millionaire entrepreneur and race-horse owner [[Terry Ramsden]] and with his money came high profile signings and the attention of the national media. In 1986–87, under new manager Tommy Coakley, Walsall narrowly missed the playoffs, but made considerable progress in the FA Cup as they defeated First Division [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] and Birmingham City and took [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] to two replays in the fifth round. Walsall earned promotion through the [[Football League Third Division|old Division Three]] play-offs in 1988, beating [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] in a replayed final. 1988–89 saw the club relegated from Division Two and Ramsden's business empire collapsed alongside the [[Tokyo Stock Exchange|Japanese Stock Exchange]]. Walsall were minutes from being taken over by Japanese Administrators and folded, but survived, again through the actions of Barrie Blower and local businessmen.

[[Image:Old Walsall FC Logo.PNG|right|thumb|The old Walsall logo]]
Further relegation followed at the end of 1989–90 as Walsall were consigned to Division Four. The club moved to the [[Bescot Stadium]] in 1990. # Introduction

Walsall Football Club, commonly known as "The Saddlers," is an English football club based in Walsall, West Midlands. Founded in 1888 as Walsall Town Swifts, the club has a rich history spanning over a century. Currently playing in League One, Walsall has seen numerous ups and downs throughout its existence, including several promotions and relegations. The club's home ground is the Banks's Stadium, which holds a capacity of 11,300 spectators. 

## History and Formation

### Early Beginnings

Walsall Football Club was originally formed in 1888 as Walsall Town Swifts, an amalgamation of Walsall Town F.C. and Walsall Swifts F.C. Both clubs had been established earlier, with Walsall Town F.C. founded in 1877 and Walsall Swifts F.C. in 1879. The newly formed Walsall Town Swifts participated in their first match, which ended in a draw against Aston Villa. This early period laid the foundation for what would become a significant presence in English football.

### Early Success and Challenges

In 1892, Walsall became one of the founder members of the Football League Second Division. However, the club faced challenges in its early years, failing to be re-elected to the Football League in 1894-95. Despite this setback, Walsall continued to compete, changing its name to Walsall F.C. and joining the Midland League. Over the years, the club has consistently strived to improve its standing in English football.

### Notable Achievements

One of Walsall's most notable achievements occurred in 1930 when they drew a crowd of 74,600 fans for an FA Cup Fourth Round match against Aston Villa. Although the match was technically a home game for Walsall, it was played at Villa Park, making it the highest attendance the club has ever experienced. Another significant moment came in 1933 when Walsall defeated Arsenal 2-0 in the FA Cup, despite Arsenal going on to win the First Division that season.

## Recent History and Development

### Promotions and Relegations

Throughout the latter half of the 20th century, Walsall experienced several periods of promotion and relegation. In 1958, following a reorganization of the Football League, Walsall became a founding member of the Fourth Division. Under the management of Bill Moore, the club achieved successive promotions, reaching the Second Division for the first time since the early 1900s. However, the club was relegated back to Division Three in 1962-63 and remained there until another demotion to the Fourth Division in 1978-79.

### Player Development

Walsall has a strong tradition of developing talented players who go on to achieve success at higher levels. Allan Clarke, Bert Williams, Phil Parkes, David Kelly, Michael Ricketts, Matty Fryatt, and Ishmel Demontagnac are among the players who have represented England or their respective countries after starting their careers at Walsall.

### Stadium and Groundshare Plans

In the 1980s, Walsall faced significant challenges, including plans to move to Birmingham and share grounds with Birmingham City. However, the town rallied behind Barrie Blower, who led a successful campaign to keep the club in Walsall. In 1986, Terry Ramsden, a wealthy businessman, purchased the club, bringing high-profile signings and national media attention. Despite initial success, Ramsden's business empire collapsed, nearly leading to the club's demise. However, local efforts saved Walsall, and the club moved to the state-of-the-art Bescot Stadium in 1990.

## Current Status

Today, Walsall Football Club continues to compete in League One, striving for promotion and maintaining its reputation as a club that develops talent. The club's nickname, "The Saddlers," reflects Walsall's historical connection to saddle manufacturing, adding a unique identity to the team. With a dedicated fan base and a rich history, Walsall remains an integral part of English football.

He made his [[Ligue 1]] debut on March 26, 1994 in a 2-0 victory against [[Angers SCO|Angers]].[http://www.lequipe.fr/Football/FootballFicheJoueur2614.html L'Equipe - Gregory Coupet profile] After three seasons, he surprisingly moved to league rival [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] (the two cities are only 80 kilometers apart, and are long-time local and national rivals). His gamble paid off as Lyon have regularly dominated [[Ligue 1|Le Championnat]] since 2002 and are also a regular fixture in the [[UEFA Champions League]]. Coupet performed a memorable double save against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] during an [[UEFA_Champions_League_2001-02|UEFA Champions League 2001-02]] match, when he first acrobatically headed an unintended lob by a defender to his own crossbar, and then immediately parried a close header by the arriving Barcelona striker [[Rivaldo]].[http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/sports/soccer/longterm/2001/uefa/champleague/firstphase/barcalyon.htm Kluivert Class Earns Barca Win Over Lyon][http://www.wldcup.com/news/2001Oct/20011010_10744_world_soccer.html Champions League - FC Barcelona 2 Olympique Lyon 0] He openly wept during the group photo before France faced [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]] in a 2003 Confederations Cup semifinal match, which had taken place just hours after the shocking death of his close friend and former Lyon teammate [[Marc-Vivien Foé]].[http://www.theage.com.au/articles/2003/06/27/1056683905680.html Cameroon player collapses, dies] Coupet credits the aftermath of Foe's death in helping him gain a new perspective on life, in the process settling his differences with Lyon after having been engaged in nasty contract imbroglios for most of the 2002-03 season, which included at one point his vowing never to play for the club again. In 2005, Coupet was voted for the first time, at age 33, into the top 10 for the [[IFFHS]] World's Best Goalkeeper Award. He finished with 43 votes, fourth behind winner [[Petr Čech]], [[Nelson de Jesus Silva|Dida]], and [[Gianluigi Buffon]], respectively. He has also twice been named Ligue 1 Keeper of the Year, in 2004 and 2005.[http://www.iffhs.de/?d847e4a95e99a54384d85fe8f55005fdcdc3bfcdc0aec70aeecf8a3c1d The World's best Goalkeeper 2005] On August 2, 2007, Coupet suffered a torn internal medial ligament in his left knee after catching his foot in the net during a training session. He underwent surgery four days later and missed the remainder of 2007, including France's final [[Euro 2008]] qualifiers. He later joked on Lyon's official television network:
"The good side...is that [France] have a rugby [[Rugby World Cup|World Cup]] coming and I’ll be able to enjoy every bit of it."[http://thestar.com.my/sports/story.asp?file=/2007/8/4/sports/18499286&sec=sports Coupet out for four months]
Coupet returned to the squad in the new year making his return in Lyon's 4-0 victory over [[Ligue 2]] side [[US Créteil-Lusitanos|Créteil]] in the [[Coupe de France]] on January 6, 2008.[http://www6.sbs.com.au/home/index.php?pid=st&cid=103251 Coupet on track for comeback] Since his return, he has played all of Lyon's matches; including the Champions League games against Manchester United. ===Atlético Madrid=== On Friday, May 23, 2008, Coupet announced that he would be playing his final game for Lyon in the French Cup final against [[Paris Saint-Germain]].[http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=776152.html?cid=rssfeed&att= Coupet to leave Lyon after Cup final] After several weeks of uncertainty, it was officially confirmed by [[Atlético Madrid]] on July 7, 2008, that Coupet would continue his career at the Spanish club, signing a contract for two seasons and signed for €1.5 million. ===Paris Saint Germain === Coupet did not play much with Atlético, which resulted in his move to [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] of [[Ligue 1]].[http://www.clubatleticodemadrid.com/en/atleticoaldia/noticias.asp?id=2664 Atlético de Madrid signs Gregory Coupet, French national team starting goalkeeper][http://www.clubatleticodemadrid.com/en/atleticoaldia/noticias.asp?id=2669 Gregory Coupet puts on the Club Atlético de Madrid jersey for the first time] On 28 November 2009, Coupet suffered from a freak, potentially career-ending injury after failing to clear a loose ball. == International career == Coupet has 34 [[cap (sport)|caps]] with [[France national football team|France]]. He made his international debut against [[Socceroos|Australia]] during France's 2001 [[FIFA Confederations Cup]]-winning campaign. He was called up for the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]] as the backup to [[Fabien Barthez]], but did not play. The following year, Coupet kept three clean sheets and conceded only three goals in five games as France won the 2003 Confederations Cup, which marked their second victory in the competition in three years. In February 2006, ''France Football'' magazine conducted a poll among its readers as to who should be France's first-choice goalie for the World Cup; Coupet received 69 percent of the votes (Barthez received 28 percent).[http://www.worldcuplatest.com/france-fans-vote-gregory-coupet-to-succeed-fabien-barthez-as-first-choice-goalkeeper-for-les-bleus.html France Fans Vote Gregory Coupet] Though Coupet started six of 10 games in the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] qualifying rounds, coach [[Raymond Domenech]] surprisingly elected Barthez as his number one, which would relegate Coupet to the bench once again. Many had expected Coupet to be chosen as the starter due to his excellent performances with [[Olympique Lyonnais]] that had contributed greatly to their streak of five Ligue 1 championships. This ultimately led to a row on May 25, 2006 between Coupet and Domenech that resulted in Coupet storming out of the team's training camp in [[Tignes]] with his family in tow, but he later returned and made amends with the coach.[http://www.rediff.com/sports/2006/may/25coupet.htm Coupet storms out after Barthez dispute] Coupet became France's number one after Barthez announced his retirement from both club and country football in August 2006.
